item.title: Light Learns to Tell Left from Right
item.description: Synthetic chiral light sculpts a three-dimensional electric field that drives left- and right-handed molecules to ionize and fragment differently.

item.title: Squaring the Shadow: Hyperbolic Cubics Find Their Spectrahedral Form
item.description: A five-variable cubic hyperbolicity cone is revealed as a spectrahedral shadow, bridging real-rooted geometry and semidefinite programming.

item.title: Diamond's Hidden Singing: Topological Surface Phonons Observed
item.description: Topological surface phonons on diamond are revealed by sum-frequency spectroscopy, where infrared lasers excite protected vibrational modes on the crystal's surface.

item.title: How Chiral Light Learns to Reveal Molecular Handedness
item.description: Counter-rotating laser fields encode a hidden topological charge that chiral perovskite powders convert into a background-free third-harmonic signal, revealing molecular handedness.

item.title: Triangulating the Impossible: Why Projective Space Needs Exponential Vertices
item.description: Every triangulation of real projective d-space demands exponentially many vertices in the square root of the dimension, because a free antipodal mirror cannot be tiled cheaply.

item.title: A Blood-Cell-Sized Detector Decodes Light's Full Story
item.description: A blood-cell-sized van der Waals junction decodes light’s color and full polarization simultaneously in a single electrically tunable pixel.

item.title: The Electron Microscope That Learned to Remember Motion
item.description: Electron tomography now reconstructs a continuous three-dimensional movie of a single heated nanoparticle as it reshapes, turning lost motion into visible time.

item.title: A Laser on a Chip Learns Quantum Logic
item.description: An integrated silicon-nitride Brillouin laser on a chip drives quantum logic gates in trapped strontium ions, shrinking the optical machinery of quantum computing.

item.title: Learning Exact Symmetry Shouldn't Be This Easy
item.description: An invariant subspace and subgroup lattice reveal how exact symmetry can be learned efficiently from data.

item.title: Splitting to Coordinate: How Roles Ignite an Information Engine
item.description: In a collective information engine, noisy social signals ignite with feedback, splitting identical agents into leaders and followers that coordinate as a whole.

item.title: Watching Atoms Decide: A Correlated Insulator Turns Metal
item.description: Time-resolved three-dimensional electron diffraction captures vanadium atoms gliding along straight paths as their paired dimers dissolve, switching the crystal from insulating to metallic.

item.title: Laws Don't Rule Alone: Mapping Physics' Hidden Ecologies
item.description: Every data-driven equation discovery method assumes (implicitly and without verification) that the target system obeys a single governing law ($K{=}1$). Here we show that this assumption is the primary bottleneck limiting scientific discovery in multi-mechanism syst...

item.title: Learning the Roads Proteins Rarely Travel
item.description: A neural probability map illuminates the rare mountain passes a protein crosses, turning seldom-traveled transitions between metastable states into visible roads.

item.title: How an Array of Flat Lenses Learns to See Color
item.description: Collaborative metalenses distribute the visible spectrum across six flat sub-lenses, and a joint non-generative reconstruction algorithm recovers sharp color images.

item.title: Watching the Five-Dimensional Weather Inside a Fusion Reactor
item.description: A neural network forecasts the five-dimensional turbulent weather inside a fusion reactor, reproducing plasma eddies and zonal flows at a fraction of the computational cost of full gyrokinetic simulations.

item.title: Regenerating Code That Refuses to Age
item.description: Design documents become the durable source of truth, as AI agents regenerate performance-modeling code from prose before each new hardware generation.

item.title: When Stars Swallow Their Own Storms
item.description: Laser-created plasma streams mimic stellar eruptions, revealing that strong magnetic fields can confine coronal mass ejections and trigger kink instabilities until the storm is swallowed by its star.

item.title: Building Memory into AI's Search for Solutions
item.description: Praxist gives AI research agents a typed evidence graph, turning scattered experiments into validated solution lineages for efficient, traceable discovery.

item.title: Vacuum Fluctuations Feel a Solid's Quantum Geometry
item.description: Zero-point fluctuations in a superconducting circuit exert a quantum geometric force on nearby solids, linking measurable repulsion and attraction to the quantum weight of the material.

item.title: A Quantum Tower Beneath CERN: Listening for Dark Matter
item.description: A hundred-metre atom interferometer in CERN's PX46 shaft would search for ultralight dark matter by measuring quantum interference of free-falling strontium atoms.

item.title: A Metal That Remembers: Breaking an Old Ferroelectric Taboo
item.description: Nitrogen-doped cubic silicon carbide becomes a ferroelectric metal: directional conduction electrons preserve a switchable bulk polarization, enabling fast, low-voltage memory devices.

item.title: Can Machines Learn the Grammar of Emergence?
item.description: An enzyme emerges layer by layer, from a low-entropy architectural skeleton to high-entropy catalytic details, revealing a learnable grammar of construction.

item.title: Painting Voltage Maps with an Exciton Sensor
item.description: An exciton sensor in a monolayer molybdenum diselenide crystal maps electrostatic potential across a bilayer semiconductor without electrical contact, revealing the intrinsic voltage landscape hidden by contact resistance.

item.title: Building a Superconducting Diode That Reverses Without a Field
item.description: A superconducting diode built from atomically thin niobium diselenide and chromium tribromide crystals carries current without resistance and flips polarity through magnetic-field history.

item.title: A Plasma Wakefield Joins the Axion Hunt
item.description: A laser-driven plasma wake replaces superconducting magnets, converting photons into axions and back into a telltale photon signal.

item.title: Leaving the Lab: A Laser Wakefield Accelerator Goes to Work
item.description: A laser wakefield accelerator survives a 72-hour stable run and a seven-month industrial trial, using compact X-ray microtomography to inspect turbine blades.

item.title: How Magnetic Black Holes Become Rapid Sirens
item.description: Magnetic black holes may emit rapid gravitational-wave whispers weeks after a merger, revealing hidden monopoles and ultralight bosons.

item.title: Learning When to Stop: Fast Readout for Atom Arrays
item.description: Adaptive photon counting lets neutral-atom processors read out qubits in microseconds, signaling each atom only until its state is clear.

item.title: How a Sharp Curl Inequality Finally Found Its Optimizers
item.description: A sharp curl inequality on the sphere is optimized by positive Killing forms, confirming Rivière's problem and proving global minimality of the Hopf map in the Faddeev-Skyrme model.

item.title: Reading a Quantum Dot's Buried Architecture
item.description: A three-dimensional atomic reconstruction reveals a lopsided core and uneven shell inside a single quantum dot, with nearly atomically abrupt internal seams.
